clue.text: Correspondence made by accident?

parts.note: two events that correspond, or match up, purely by chance rather than design

explanation.surface: A letter that got sent by mistake, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' looks like letters in the post, but here it means two things matching up.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance agreement of events in time or circumstance is exactly a correspondence nobody planned.

clue.text: Opportunity to get money for part of the church

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra), standing for money

explanation.surface: A church sees an opening to raise funds.
explanation.definitionFit: The area around the altar reserved for clergy and choir is a named section of a church building.

clue.text: Bury, in the meantime, I'm leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the letters of the word I'm go away from the longer word

parts.note: in the interim means in the meantime
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they will bury something while they are on their way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a grave is to bury it; a formal synonym.

clue.text: One in the club has whip-round for cheese

indicators.note: round says the whip's word goes around the clubber's word

parts.note: the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
someone who belongs to a club is a member

explanation.surface: A club member organises a collection to buy cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but splits into whip (CAT) and round, the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, creamy French variety from Normandy is a well-known type of cheese.

clue.text: A little upset when given the facts

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly upset on learning the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as mild distress but turns A TAD around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Information gathered for reference or analysis is a set of facts and figures.

clue.text: Turn once set to music

indicators.note: set means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A single dance move choreographed to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like 'set to music' but is the anagram signal on TURN ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy piano piece evoking the night, as by Chopin, is a kind of music.

clue.text: Once article for sale comes up, applaud

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: in a down clue comes up means the word rises, read from the bottom

parts.note: a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: An auction lot appears and the bidders clap.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise enthusiastically is synonymous with applaud in its figurative sense.

clue.text: We back a cowboy film

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Fans declare their support for a cowboy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it is the noun, the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre film set in the American frontier with cowboys is the classic example.

clue.text: If given a rise, live somewhere warm

indicators.note: in a down clue being raised means reading the word upward, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: to live somewhere is to reside

explanation.surface: With a pay rise, someone could afford to live somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a rise' suggests a pay increase but lifts IF upwards to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The area by a hearth is a cosy, heated spot in a home.

clue.text: Will it shoot itself?

parts.note: a self-loading gun keeps firing on its own once triggered

explanation.surface: A question about a gun going off by itself, like a suicide joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm that reloads and fires repeatedly by itself is described by this word.

clue.text: Make jet return excursions

indicators.note: return means the word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: to spirt (spurt) is to send out a jet of liquid

explanation.surface: An airline brings its jet back from short holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' looks like an aircraft but is a squirt of liquid; SPIRT is a variant of spurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Short journeys for pleasure, such as day outings, are excursions.

clue.text: Plate showing church beside Holy Father's home

indicators.note: beside says one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: the Pope, the Holy Father, lives in Rome

explanation.surface: A collection plate displayed in a church next to the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' looks like a church collection plate but means a metal coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromium coating on metal is a form of plating, as on car bumpers.

clue.text: A sweet dog Bill Sikes had

definitions.meaning: a hard round peppermint humbug with stripes is a traditional British boiled sweet
in Dickens's Oliver Twist the villain Bill Sikes owns a bull terrier of this name

explanation.surface: A villain's dog and a confection side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a striped mint candy and the famous Dickensian dog carry this name.

clue.text: He is taken in by a girl — who fluttered them?

indicators.note: taken in by says the first word goes inside the girl's word

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A man is fooled by a flirtatious girl batting her eyelids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled; here it is the containment signal. The definition points at what the girl fluttered.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirt flutters her eyelashes, so these are the things she fluttered.

clue.text: Beach shoes are adjusted for it

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Shoes are modified for walking on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of land along the sea is a synonym for the coast's sandy edge.

clue.text: Doing nothing on the front line?

definitions.meaning: idleness, a lack of any activity
read as two words, a soldier at the front is ...

explanation.surface: Idling on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as IN ACTION, fighting at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness and inertia are the plain meaning; the split reading describes soldiers fighting.

clue.text: Tom perhaps needs a pick-me-up, as in a coma

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example
a tonic is a restorative drink

explanation.surface: A sluggish cat needs reviving as if comatose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of stupor with rigid immobility resembles being in a coma.

clue.text: Can start out to do business

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm can set out to trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a deal or carry on commerce is to do business.

clue.text: Flowers required by company for shipping

definitions.note: ships collectively; the answer names the vessels themselves

parts.note: asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A firm needs flowers sent by freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' suggests blooms but could also be rivers; here it is the blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Small vessels plying trade along a coast are a class of merchant ship.

clue.text: Wine cash bill is incorrect — fifty short

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters are wrongly arranged and must be reshuffled
short says the bill is lacking the fifty, so that letter is removed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A diner disputes a wine bill fifty pounds out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L (fifty) from CASH BILL, then shuffle the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white Burgundy from the Chablis region is a well-known wine.

clue.text: Current classmates

definitions.meaning: a flow of water, as in a brook
in British schools pupils grouped by ability form a set of classmates

explanation.surface: Present-day schoolfellows.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools stream pupils, grouping them by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow of water is a current, and an ability group at school is the same word.

clue.text: Meets us in transit for an essential event

indicators.note: in transit means on the move, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Someone meets us on the move for an unmissable occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one simply has to attend or watch is unmissable, an essential event.

clue.text: Tenacious advocate

definitions.meaning: a supporter or follower of a cause

explanation.surface: A dogged campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sticking firmly; as a noun, a follower or supporter.

clue.text: It does, with time

parts.note: the words does and time end in the same sound, so one chimes with the other

explanation.surface: Something happens if you wait long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' must be read as the plural of doe, which chimes with 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that share an end sound, like these two, form a poetic match.

clue.text: Blood making clot doctor assist

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor helps when blood clots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb, to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically the term means stagnation of blood flow, which leads to clotting.

clue.text: Works are held up by it — one in 25, for instance, is continental

definitions.text: Works are held up by it
definitions.meaning: books, literary works, stand on a ledge for them

definitions.text: one in 25, for instance, is continental
definitions.meaning: the answer to 25-down, a continent, has its own submerged coastal ledge, as every continent does

explanation.surface: Building works delayed, while a European tells us something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests delayed but means supported. The continental type is the seabed fringe of a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge for books and the sea-floor margin of a landmass share this name.

clue.text: Somewhere in atlas, I assume it's included

indicators.note: included says the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A place one assumes is shown in the atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a place, so it is a deliberately vague example of somewhere.

clue.text: Licensed carrier

parts.note: a goods vehicle that needs an operator's licence to carry freight on the road

explanation.surface: An airline with permission to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests an airline; here it is a road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy goods vehicle, called a truck in America, carries loads under licence.

clue.text: Not so busy types told to go — a busy type's coming round

indicators.note: coming round says the first pieces go around the next

parts.note: a bee is proverbially busy; read as plural
sent means ordered to go

explanation.surface: Idlers are dismissed as a hard worker arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy type's' gives BEES, the 's read as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are not present are hardly busy at their posts; a jokey description.

clue.text: One is admitted after this transport charge

parts.note: to entrance is to transport with delight
a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: Paying a bus fare before being let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like vehicles but is the verb, to enrapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying the admission price is what lets a visitor in.
